<text x="130.0" y="322.0" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">columns = successive periods; each row = one phase of the cycle</text>
</g>
<g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
<rect x="187.0" y="177.0" width="92.0" height="122.0" rx="3" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.4"/>
<text x="340.0" y="198.0" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#dc2626" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">a 2-D kernel across a few columns sees whether the cycle really repeats:</text>
<text x="340.0" y="220.0" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#dc2626" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">harmonics are periodicity, W2's source. Five of them, p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 —</text>
<text x="340.0" y="242.0" font-size="16" font-weight="600" fill="#dc2626" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">coprime, so they tile different fundamental frequencies without overlap</text>
<text x="340.0" y="276.0" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">the MSD is the other family: 1-D, at ×1, ×2, ×4 downsampling — long-range continuity</text>
<text x="340.0" y="300.0" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="auto">in a tone language the period is lexical: this discriminator is checking our words</text>
</g>
</svg>
